text:
incident-bot: [PAGE] P2 - Elevated P95 latency for hosted inference (us-west-2). Detected 21:02 UTC. Affected route: /v1/generate (redwood-small-quant). Auto-escalation threshold hit.
ops-oncall: acked, I'm on it. Pulling traces and recent deploys. paging channel -> #incidents. tagging @alice_nguyen for runtime changes.
alice_nguyen: oncall here. seeing a spike in queue depth on the batcher around 20:58. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~92% to 30% for redwood-small-quant. correlates with a deploy at 20:56 that touched cache invalidation logic.
miguel: grabbing metrics — p50 65ms -> 70ms, p95 1.8s -> 4.3s at peak, error rate up 0.7% (timeouts). I'll open a short grafana link: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123.
carla: quick sanity: which pods are showing regen? looks like two worker pools spiking memory and GC. I suspect a combination: cache misses causing increased token decoding + larger batch windows = longer latency.
ops-oncall: can we try rollback of the KV cache change to confirm? If rollback too slow, propose to force cache bypass for that model to avoid cache miss penalty.
alice_nguyen: preparing rollback of cache invalidation PR. If rollback ETA > 10m, I'll patch a hotfix to bypass caching for redwood-small-quant via runtime flag.
ops-oncall: agree. Alice, prioritize bypass patch first (safer). Keep rollback ready.
alice_nguyen: applying hotfix now:
```bash
# set env on pool redwood-quant-pool
kubectl set env deployment/redwood-quant-pool RUNTIME_FORCE_CACHE_BYPASS=redwood-small-quant --namespace=hosting-us-west-2
```
alice_nguyen: hotfix applied, rolling to 3 pods. watching.
miguel: tailing traces — after hotfix p95 trending down from 4.3s -> 1.1s within 60s. errors dropping. plotting token throughput: stable.
carla: good signal. batching queue sizes normalized. Looks like cache invalidation produced a stampede where many requests recomputed KV and bumped batch windows. Batching config allowed bigger max_wait when queue filled; that amplified tail latency.
sre_lead: nice mitigation. Keep hotfix until we have postmortem. We'll need: rollback diff analysis, batching config guardrails, and a canary for cache invalidation changes.
product_rachel: any customer impact? I see two enterprise apps reported slow responses and one webhook retry loop. Customer success, please confirm and message customers.
cust_success_tom: contacted both affected accounts (Acme and HelixSoft). Acme saw ~10 failed requests, HelixSoft reported degraded UX for ~7 minutes. Provided summary and ETA for full postmortem. They appreciated the proactive updates.
ops-oncall: logging timeline for incident timeline doc. Initial detect 21:02 UTC, hotfix applied 21:07 UTC, partial recovery 21:09 UTC, full recovery 21:12 UTC.
alice_nguyen: creating remediation branch with two changes: 1) revert risky cache invalidation behavior and 2) tighten batcher max_wait and max_batch_tokens for that pool. Will open PR shortly.
carla: suggest automated safety net: when cache miss rate spikes > 20% for > 1m, temporarily limit max_wait to 50ms and reduce batch size to avoid HL blocking. We should implement this in the serving runtime not just configs.
sre_lead: agree. Add as action item. Also we need a pre-merge canary that runs perf tests exercising KV invalidation on a synthetic workload.
ops-oncall: handoff: I need to pass to @night_oncall for 22:00-06:00 UTC. Night_oncall, you're up, incident currently mitigated by hotfix. Keep patch in place until PR and canary validated.
night_oncall: ack. I'll monitor for regressions and keep PS engaged if customers escalate.
product_rachel: scheduling postmortem: propose tomorrow 15:00 UTC (60m). I'll invite eng-runtime, SRE, product, and CS. Does that work?
sre_lead: works for me. Please add an action item to track remediation in JIRA. Suggest ticket RED-3421 for tracking and link in postmortem.
alice_nguyen: PR opened: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/789 — revert + batcher guard. Running CI, requesting reviewers: @carla @sre_lead.
miguel: added metric panels: KV cache hit rate, batcher queue depth, p95 by model, and a new error-type breakdown. Dashboards linked in PR description.
cust_success_tom: sent follow-up email to customers with interim mitigation summary and promise for full postmortem. Both requested timeline; they said the quick fix helped.
sre_lead: action items (assign owners):
- RED-3421: Revert cache invalidation logic + deploy safe replacement (owner: alice_nguyen, due: 2026-03-18)
- RED-3422: Implement batcher emergency throttling (owner: carla, due: 2026-03-22)
- RED-3423: Canary/perf test for KV invalidation changes (owner: miguel, due: 2026-03-20)
- RED-3424: Add pre-deploy diff check for quantized model parameter changes (owner: sre_lead, due: 2026-03-25)
- RED-3425: Customer comms and postmortem doc (owner: product_rachel + cust_success_tom, due: 2026-03-18)
sre_lead: please log these in JIRA and link back here. I'll treat this as major incident follow-up.
alice_nguyen: noted and will attach the perf traces to RED-3421.
carla: quick note — also add an observability alert for sudden drop in KV hit-rate (threshold 40% sustained 30s). I'll add to RED-3422 or create separate.
ops-oncall: closing the live incident now. Hotfix remains; don't merge rollback until the canary passes. Postmortem meeting scheduled. Thanks all for fast response :thumbsup:.
incident-bot: Incident marked resolved by ops-oncall at 21:12 UTC. Severity: P2. Linked ticket: RED-3421.
sre_lead: closing comment — let's make sure the postmortem includes a short customer impact summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis (KV invalidation bug + permissive batching), and concrete remediation plan + owners.
product_rachel: I'll create the postmortem doc and share draft in #postmortems before meeting.
cust_success_tom: leaving thread, will update customers when postmortem is ready.
night_oncall: monitoring overnight, will escalate if we see any recurrence.
ops-oncall: last note: retained logs and traces snapshot saved to s3://redwood-incidents/2149998888/ for future analysis.
